issue.title: bug: Apps removed from Dynamic Sections when window minimised.

repository.name: homarr
repository.description: A modern and easy to use dashboard. 40+ integrations. 20K+ icons built in. Authentication out of the box. No YAML, drag and drop configuration.

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

With apps placed within a Dynamic Section on a board, when the window is minimised, the apps are removed from the dynamic section and displayed alongside the dynamic section. The dynamic section displayed is a blank box alongside the apps. Tested in both Edge & Chrome

NB: Minimised photo shows Plex missing but it is outside of view. Also, in a mobile browser, the Dynamic Section doesn't work and contains lots of issues i.e. arrangement and sizes of widgets.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73b0db19-cd54-4ed2-ba60-90de240b54e0)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fc7a1cb-13f5-4eee-b9ca-257773ce8d84)

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a board with a dynamic section.
- Add 3 apps within the dynamic section and save.
- In view, minimise the window size. Apps will remove themselves from the dynamic section.

### Impact

Low - Just don't use the screen minimised!

### Additional information

Installed using Proxmox Helper Script

### Version

1.16.0

### Installation method

Other (describe in "additional information")

### Browser

Chrome

body:
We need to have a chat about this functionallity. In theory it is expected behaviour as we can not know where you want the item placed for the other layouts and it could be possible that you want to have the structure different between multiple layouts. I think there might be a good solution with having one base layout and generating the layout of the other sizes automatically (with an algorithm that we already use when adding layouts) and maybe a second one that always moves the items you move to the same section (if there is enough space, which might not be the case for certain dynamic sections)

What do you think @manuel-rw ?

Just my 2 cents. I really don't think that should be how it is designed. I could be wrong, but I'm thinking most people assign categories based on what the app does. Example, you might have one category that has media(stuff like Jellyfin or Plex). Another category might have infrastructure. Things like docker and uptime kuma. I really don't think most people are categorizing them differently on mobile vs desktop. And on top of that, there's no simple way to change the actual layout for the desktop from mobile. 

And what I would love to see, if it is even possible, is to just have one layout, and it automatically adjusts everything based on the screen size. Basically just try to keep the icons a certain size(or a range of size) and just resize things automatically. And option to have something like that instead of manually creating layouts for every size of screen I might use would be really nice.

I came here to report this as a bug, not expecting it to be intended behaviour. 

I too use categories for different purposes. Like transport. I deliberately made the widget bigger in the transport section too, which is not only not staying larger on mobile, but it comes out of the category. This behaviour is very strange. 

As you can see it doesn't even keep the order. On desktop, in the category it's Proxmox, Departures, Departures. On the mobile it's Departures, Departures, Proxmox.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/031d3256-d792-47f8-a037-f280146c6ea0)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1272757b-0c7e-455d-a0db-2b1fa1a5a8f2)

issue.title: bug: Items in categories on

repository.name: homarr
repository.description: A modern and easy to use dashboard. 40+ integrations. 20K+ icons built in. Authentication out of the box. No YAML, drag and drop configuration.

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

As well as the odd behaviour of things coming out of categories when viewing on mobile... (see https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/issues/2861)

I've taken everything out of categories and was expecting it to stay in the same order. I have a 12 column desktop and a 4 column mobile of the same board.

Even across rows I expect them to stay in the same order, but instead on desktop I've got (the last 2 are placeholders which I hoped would force the next line to stay in it's next row of 12 when on mobile):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d31d58a-6909-4bb2-8400-2b6d0ef105c1)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af86785c-0a2f-47d9-820c-a0e21f9cf3c4)

The 2 Hi's should be on row 3, and the trains on row 4, but on mobile they swap.

This can't be intended behaviour, surely?

Thank you kindly :)

### Steps to reproduce

Create many items, and watch on mobile as they go out of order

### Impact

No workaround I'm aware of, this doesn't make it unusable but it is unpleasant to use

### Additional information

Installed from Proxmox Helper Scripts

### Version

1.20.0

### Installation method

Other (describe in "additional information")

### Browser

Firefox

body:
I came here because of the same issue with dynamic sections. The odd thing is, in my older dynamic sections, the apps stay in. Only in the ones I created today, the apps drop out. I don't remember which version I created the older dynamic sections with.

I'm basically on the fence, waiting for Homarr to be production ready while still using dashy. So I fire up my container every so and so many months and check what has changed.

Actually, Homarr seems to remember all app -> dynamic section relations per breakpoint from before today/yesterday. I also moved some apps between sections and when I reduce the canvas size, not only the new ones jump out of their dynamic sections but also apps which I moved from one to another jump back to where they were before...

In my opinion that doesn't make sense. @simpat1zq is right. People assign apps to dynamic sections or categories based on function - or maybe physical location or topic. In any case, by criteria which don't change with the screen/canvas size.
And I'm fairly sure, nobody wants to edit possibly multiple dashboards for multiple breakpoints. And keep multiple breakpoints updated at every change. That amount of configuration work would defeat the purpose of a dashboard app -> fast, simple access to a large number of services.

I'm not sure if this would be possible, but I think one way you might be able to handle this is to limit how small the icons can get in a particular layout. For example, I have my layout set to 9 columns. If I make the browser smaller(which basically simulates a smaller screen), then the icons keep getting smaller to a point that they are useless. But, if there were a setting that limits how small the icons can get, and instead simply reduces the number of columns to prevent them from getting too small, I really think it would work perfectly on any size screen. 

I'm not sure how hard that would be to implement or how well it would work, but I feel that if you can get something like that working then homarr would be great for people that use it across multiple devices.

i have the same issue. But it's not only on mobile. Below are screenhots of my desktop Firefox 153.0.4 (64-bits) My responsive layout settings - small, 0 , columns 4 - medium, 600, columns 6 - large, 1200, columns 10 **Layed out good. Uses "large"** **Faulty layed out. Uses "medium"** **Faulty layed out. Uses "small"** ! The runtime behaviour even changes when i enter the layouts in reverse order, so starting with 'large'

This issue has been open for a really long time, so I think it's just not a common use case for other people. That said, you throw this into AI and I think it might be able to generate a CSS that will fix it.

> This issue has been open for a really long time, so I think it's just not a common use case for other people. That said, you throw this into AI and I think it might be able to generate a CSS that will fix it.

Although many people who use dashboards like this tend to be of the nerdy type, I also wonder how many get this issue and simply move on to something else, without coming here to Github. Maybe many people, many nobody. Either way the issue is disappointing and I've been using Flame happily for a while now - not as pretty, but adapts to any screen size perfectly, keeping things in order
